papers.title: Scope-WM: Scoped Computation for Efficient Visual World Models
papers.abstract: Visual world models enable robotic planning by predicting future observations, but dense latent-state propagation and sample-intensive trajectory optimization incur high inference latency and peak memory usage, limiting real-time deployment on resource-constrained platforms. Existing sparse world-model acceleration methods either rely on unguided token sparsification, which may discard planning-relevant information and restrict achievable sparsity, or introduce heavy auxiliary modules and cumbersome multi-stage training pipelines. In this work, we present Scope-WM, an efficient visual world model that scopes computation to prediction-relevant latent regions and promising action sequences. Scope-WM distills prediction relevance into a lightweight action-conditioned selector and applies full dynamics prediction only to a compact subset of selected tokens. It updates the remaining tokens using a compact summary of foreground states and their changes, allowing the background to perceive foreground dynamics without costly token-to-token interactions. During planning, Scope-WM preserves and reuses high-quality action sequences discovered during the initial MPC search, focusing subsequent search under reduced rollout budgets. The resulting pipeline requires only a one-off selector distillation followed by a single joint training stage for the sparse world model. On the challenging Push-T task, Scope-WM reduces peak GPU memory usage and planning time to $18.1\%$ and $14.3\%$ of those of dense DINO-WM, respectively, corresponding to a $6.97\times$ planning speedup, while maintaining competitive task performance. Further evaluations across five diverse visual planning tasks demonstrate the general applicability of Scope-WM. Code is available at https://github.com/ChunZheng2022/Scope-WM.
papers.summary_cn: 本文针对基于视觉世界模型的机器人规划中潜状态传播和采样式 MPC 计算成本高的问题，提出 Scope-WM。该方法在三个层面分配计算：使用蒸馏相关性选择（DRS）根据视觉状态、控制状态和动作选择需要完整动力学预测的少量标记；使用前景-变化量背景更新（FDBU）通过前景状态及其运动变化的汇总信息轻量更新背景标记；使用精英库交叉熵方法（EB-CEM）在初始 MPC 步骤投入更多采样，并在后续步骤复用高质量动作序列。实验基于 DINO-WM，在 PointMaze、Wall、Push-T、Rope 和 Granular 五项任务上进行。Push-T 上最激进的 32 标记配置将规划时间和峰值 GPU 内存分别降至稠密基线的 14.3% 和 18.1%，实现 6.97 倍加速，同时成功率为 88%；较宽松的 98 标记配置成功率达到 94%。消融实验表明，DRS、FDBU 和 EB-CEM 分别有助于相关标记选择、背景状态维护和低预算轨迹搜索。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 将高效视觉世界模型规划表述为三层计算分配问题，涵盖预测相关标记选择、前景感知的背景更新和轨迹搜索预算分配。 2. 提出 DRS，通过从完整标记教师模型中蒸馏预测相关性，利用轻量级动作条件选择器确定需要完整动力学预测的标记，并仅需一次选择器蒸馏。 3. 提出 FDBU，利用前景状态和前景变化量的汇总上下文，以轻量级门控残差更新背景标记，避免稠密的前景-背景标记交互。 4. 提出 EB-CEM，在初始 MPC 搜索中使用更大的采样预算，并将高质量动作序列存入精英库，在后续低预算搜索中复用和扰动这些序列。 5. 在五个视觉规划任务上验证了方法的效率-性能权衡，并在 Push-T 上实现显著的规划时间和显存降低。
papers.relevance_cn: 该论文与研究重点直接相关，核心对象是用于机器人闭环规划的视觉世界模型。它通过动作条件的预测相关性选择实现状态和动作依赖的稀疏计算，通过前景动力学摘要实现低成本潜状态更新，并通过精英动作序列复用减少后续 MPC 搜索开销。这些设计对应稀疏注意力或稀疏 token 计算、缓存/轨迹复用、实时推理和闭环视觉模拟。方法不是视频生成或视频扩散模型，也不是自回归像素级长视频生成；其预测对象是 DINOv2 特征空间中的未来视觉潜状态，主要目标是提高动作条件视觉世界模型的规划效率。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文在 Rope 任务上的稀疏模型性能明显低于稠密 DINO-WM：最佳 Scope-WM 的 Chamfer Distance 为 0.71，而 DINO-WM 为 0.41，说明在更复杂的可变形动力学场景中，稀疏前景预测和汇总式背景更新可能损失重要信息。更激进的稀疏配置也会带来一定性能下降，例如 Push-T 的 32 标记配置成功率为 88%，低于稠密模型的 90%，而 98 标记配置为 94%。DRS 依赖预先训练的稠密 DINO-WM 教师和一次蒸馏，FDBU 使用前景状态与变化量的汇总表示，可能无法完整表达复杂的标记间关系。实验主要基于五项离线视觉规划任务和有限的 GPU 平台，论文未明确说明在真实机器人、更多样的长时域任务、不同视觉编码器或大规模实时部署中的表现。该方法的训练和推理开销、超参数敏感性及其与视频扩散或生成式世界模型的比较，论文未明确说明。
papers.abstract_cn: 视觉世界模型通过预测未来观测来支持机器人规划，但稠密潜状态传播和高样本量轨迹优化会带来较高的推理延迟与峰值内存使用，限制其在资源受限平台上的实时部署。现有稀疏世界模型加速方法要么依赖无引导的标记稀疏化，可能丢弃与规划相关的信息并限制可实现的稀疏程度；要么引入复杂的辅助模块和繁琐的多阶段训练流程。本文提出 Scope-WM，一种高效的视觉世界模型，将计算范围限定在与预测相关的潜在区域和有前景的动作序列上。Scope-WM 将预测相关性蒸馏到一个轻量级的动作条件选择器中，仅对选定的少量标记执行完整动力学预测。对于其余标记，模型利用前景状态及其变化的紧凑摘要进行更新，使背景能够感知前景动力学，同时避免昂贵的标记间交互。在规划过程中，Scope-WM 保留并复用初始模型预测控制（MPC）搜索中发现的高质量动作序列，在减少后续 rollout 预算的情况下集中进行搜索。该流程只需进行一次选择器蒸馏，随后对稀疏世界模型进行单阶段联合训练。在具有挑战性的 Push-T 任务上，相比稠密 DINO-WM，Scope-WM 将峰值 GPU 内存使用量和规划时间分别降至其 18.1% 和 14.3%，对应 6.97 倍的规划加速，同时保持具有竞争力的任务性能。在五个不同的视觉规划任务上的进一步评估展示了 Scope-WM 的普适性。代码已公开于 https://github.com/ChunZheng2022/Scope-WM。

papers.title: DyMD: Preserving Interaction Dynamics through Distribution Matching Distillation in Few-Step Video World Models
papers.abstract: Large video diffusion models offer expressive priors for embodied prediction and learning, yet their many-step sampling remains costly for interactive downstream use. Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) enables few-step video generation, but can suppress robot--object motion while preserving visual quality. Examining DMD's teacher and fake-score signals, we find that weak re-noising keeps the teacher posterior concentrated near motion-deficient rollouts, limiting motion-restoring guidance. Meanwhile, stronger-motion rollouts tend to incur larger fake-score fitting errors, which can hinder the generator's learning of interaction dynamics. We propose DyMD, a DMD framework that adapts both teacher supervision and critic fitting to the evolving student. Temporal affinity--conditioned re-noise sampling adapts the timestep distribution to each rollout's current interaction fidelity by mixing the base schedule with a teacher prior motivated by local posterior variation, thereby balancing motion recovery and appearance refinement. To better track stronger-motion rollouts, dynamics-guided fake-score tracking uses a noise-conditioned predictor to estimate noise-relative fitting difficulty from latent temporal dynamics, then upweights predicted-hard rollouts in the critic loss. Using DyMD, we distill a 14B teacher into a four-step 1.3B student with no auxiliary modules at inference. On embodied-video benchmarks, the student improves R-Bench task adherence by $9.6$ percentage points and PAI-Bench-G Domain score by $5.1$ points over Base DMD while maintaining comparable visual quality. As a backbone for downstream action planning, our student achieves 34% mean success across two WorldArena tasks, compared with 16% for Base DMD.
papers.summary_cn: 本文研究DMD将大型视频扩散教师蒸馏为少步视频世界模型时交互动力学退化的问题。作者发现，弱重新加噪会使教师后验锁定在运动不足的学生轨迹附近，而运动较强的轨迹又更难被伪评分模型拟合。DyMD通过时间亲和度条件化的重新加噪采样，为交互保真度较低的轨迹增加教师先验采样；同时利用潜变量时间动力学预测噪声相对拟合难度，并提高困难轨迹在判别器训练中的权重。将14B PF-Wan教师蒸馏为四步1.3B学生后，DyMD在R-Bench、PAI-Bench-G和EZS-Bench上改善了交互保真度，并在WorldArena闭环动作规划中将平均成功率从16%提升至34%，且推理无需额外模块。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 分析DMD中教师监督和伪评分拟合对交互动力学退化的影响，指出教师侧模式锁定和运动相关的判别器拟合困难是关键障碍。2. 提出时间亲和度条件化的重新加噪采样，将教师速度转向先验与基础时间步调度混合，并依据每条学生轨迹当前的交互保真度自适应分配采样概率。3. 提出动力学引导的伪评分跟踪，通过噪声条件预测器从VAE潜变量时间动力学估计相对拟合难度，在固定判别器更新预算下对困难轨迹进行加权。4. 在四步、1.3B学生模型上验证方法，在多个具身视频基准和WorldArena下游动作规划任务中取得优于Base DMD的结果。
papers.relevance_cn: 本文与视频生成和视频扩散高度相关，核心目标是将14B视频扩散教师压缩为四步1.3B生成器，并降低少步采样造成的运动和交互动力学损失。它直接涉及实时或低延迟视频生成中的蒸馏、少步采样、时间步自适应分配和伪评分跟踪。作为视频世界模型，DyMD生成的视觉未来可用于具身预测和闭环动作规划；WorldArena结果表明，保留机器人—物体交互动力学能够提升下游闭环决策。论文没有重点讨论自回归、因果或流式生成，也未提出显式的稀疏注意力或缓存复用机制。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文明确指出，教师速度转向曲线依赖具体教师模型和采样调度，更换教师时必须重新估计。方法训练阶段还依赖冻结的V-JEPA特征编码器、教师模型、伪评分模型和难度预测器，训练流程较复杂，尽管推理时不需要辅助模块。实验主要基于PF-Wan教师、RoVid-X数据和三个具身视频基准，并使用四步、81帧的1.3B双向学生模型，因此对其他教师、数据分布、视频长度及因果或流式场景的泛化能力尚未充分验证。论文未明确说明真实机器人部署中的计算开销、延迟和安全性影响。
papers.abstract_cn: 大型视频扩散模型提供了用于具身预测和学习的丰富先验，但其多步采样对交互式下游应用而言成本高昂。分布匹配蒸馏（DMD）能够实现少步视频生成，但在保持视觉质量的同时可能抑制机器人与物体之间的运动。通过分析DMD中的教师信号和伪评分信号，我们发现，较弱的重新加噪会使教师后验集中在运动不足的轨迹附近，从而限制恢复运动的引导能力。同时，运动更强的轨迹往往会产生更大的伪评分拟合误差，这可能妨碍生成器学习交互动力学。我们提出DyMD，一种使教师监督和判别器拟合都适应不断演化的学生模型的DMD框架。时间亲和度条件化的重新加噪采样通过将基础调度与受局部后验变化启发的教师先验混合，根据每条轨迹当前的交互保真度调整时间步分布，从而平衡运动恢复与外观细化。为更好地跟踪运动更强的轨迹，动力学引导的伪评分跟踪器使用噪声条件预测器，根据潜变量时间动力学估计相对于噪声的拟合难度，并在判别器损失中提高预测困难轨迹的权重。使用DyMD，我们将一个14B教师模型蒸馏为一个四步、1.3B的学生模型，推理时无需额外辅助模块。在具身视频基准上，该学生模型相较于Base DMD将R-Bench任务遵循度提高了9.6个百分点，将PAI-Bench-G Domain分数提高了5.1个百分点，同时保持了相当的视觉质量。作为下游动作规划的骨干模型，该学生模型在两个WorldArena任务上取得了34%的平均成功率，而Base DMD为16%。

papers.title: In-Flight KV Cache with Clean Anchors for Faster Autoregressive Video Diffusion
papers.abstract: Few-step autoregressive video diffusion generates a long video by splitting the video into temporal chunks and generating chunk-by-chunk, each through a short sequence of denoising stages. To memorize chunks that are already generated, previous methods reconstruct a clean or less-noisy key--value (KV) cache by additional forwards to build the cache without advancing an output latent. However, every denoising forward itself already computes the in-flight KV of the current chunk. We introduce FlashForward, which directly reuses this cache to avoid the heavy cache-update-only model forwards. After the current chunk completes one denoising stage, its stage-specific cache is already available for the next chunk. Assigning one GPU to each stage therefore lets different chunks occupy different stages concurrently. This early availability has a quality cost: the resulting stage-matched history is noisy, causing appearance and motion drift among chunks. To complement it, FlashForward produces sparse auxiliary clean anchor latents before the corresponding region is generated so the generation trajectories can be stabilized by this two-sided conditioning. The two memories operate at different temporal scales: sparse clean anchor KV supplies coarse, long-range two-sided structural guidance, while dense stage-matched history preserves fine, recent evolution. With up to four GPUs, FlashForward runs $1.16$--$1.69\times$ faster than HiAR and $1.42$--$2.92\times$ faster than Self-Forcing for 16 FPS videos of 20 seconds or longer across 1.3B and 14B backbone scales at 480p and 720p. On VBench, for the 1.3B model at 480p, it achieves higher scores and remains stable at longer durations, demonstrating that FlashForward generates high-quality and temporally consistent videos across durations of 20s, 35s and 65s at a much faster generation speed.
papers.summary_cn: 论文提出 FlashForward，一种面向少步自回归视频扩散的高效生成框架。它复用普通去噪前向产生的阶段匹配 KV 缓存，使每次计算既推进当前视频片段又为后续片段提供状态，从而在多 GPU 上形成跨去噪阶段的波流水线。针对阶段匹配历史噪声较大、容易造成外观和运动漂移的问题，框架由规划器预先生成稀疏干净锚点，并与近期稠密历史结合进行双侧条件。规划器和渲染器共享骨干网络，通过监督微调和自滚动蒸馏训练。在 1.3B/14B、480p/720p 设置下，方法显著降低长视频生成延迟，并在 VBench 长视频评测中保持较好的质量和时间一致性。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出一种跨片段状态契约：每个普通渲染去噪前向在推进当前片段的同时发布阶段匹配 KV，避免仅用于缓存更新的额外前向，并支持不同去噪阶段在多 GPU 上形成波流水线。2. 提出时间尺度互补的记忆设计：稀疏干净锚点 KV 提供粗粒度、长程、双侧结构约束，阶段匹配的渲染历史提供近期的细粒度外观和运动信息。3. 设计共享骨干的规划器—渲染器架构，以角色嵌入和 LoRA 适配器区分两种 temporal dependency，并通过真实视频监督微调和自滚动分布蒸馏训练。4. 在 1.3B 和 14B 模型、480p 和 720p 视频上验证了速度优势，并在 1.3B、480p 的 VBench 及长视频测试中取得较高质量和稳定性。
papers.relevance_cn: 论文与研究重点高度相关。它直接研究自回归、少步、长视频扩散生成，并通过复用在途 KV 缓存降低生成延迟。阶段匹配历史使相邻视频片段能够跨去噪阶段流水并行，属于缓存复用和多 GPU 实时化优化；规划器预先生成稀疏锚点、渲染器进行因果生成，则提供了面向长时序一致性的双侧结构引导。方法支持流式生成，并在 20 秒、35 秒和 65 秒视频上评估，具体体现了长视频生成、因果依赖管理、并行执行和 KV 缓存设计之间的结合。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文明确指出：该方法面向长序列、少步、多 GPU 生成，规划器和流水线预热会削弱短视频的收益，单 GPU 推理无法利用波流水线并行。训练数据仅包含真实世界视频，使模型偏向写实内容，可能限制其在动画和其他风格化领域的表现。方法使用固定的锚点步长和条件窗口，并采用较为基础的训练方案；放宽固定的干净锚点状态假设和自适应锚点选择仍属于未来工作。此外，锚点位置若直接作为最终输出会产生周期性接缝，因此需要重新生成锚点位置。仅使用阶段匹配历史会产生严重闪烁，而更密集地使用干净历史和未来信息会带来较高延迟。论文未明确说明其在更多硬件配置、更多数据分布及非写实内容上的泛化性能。
papers.abstract_cn: 少步自回归视频扩散通过将视频划分为时间片段，并逐片段生成长视频；每个片段都经过一小段去噪阶段序列。为记忆已经生成的片段，现有方法通过额外的前向计算重建干净或低噪声的键值（KV）缓存，在不推进输出潜变量的情况下构建缓存。然而，每次去噪前向本身已经计算了当前片段的在途 KV。我们提出 FlashForward，直接复用这一缓存，从而避免代价高昂的、仅用于更新缓存的模型前向计算。当前片段完成一个去噪阶段后，其特定于该阶段的缓存已可供下一个片段使用。因此，为每个阶段分配一块 GPU，就能让不同片段并发处于不同阶段。这种提前可用性会带来质量代价：由此产生的阶段匹配历史带有噪声，导致片段之间出现外观和运动漂移。为此，FlashForward 在相应区域生成之前产生稀疏的辅助干净锚点潜变量，通过双侧条件稳定生成轨迹。两种记忆作用于不同的时间尺度：稀疏的干净锚点 KV 提供粗粒度、长程的双侧结构引导，而稠密的阶段匹配历史保留近期的细粒度演化信息。在最多使用四块 GPU 时，对于 480p 和 720p、1.3B 和 14B 两种骨干模型，针对时长至少 20 秒的 16 FPS 视频，FlashForward 比 HiAR 快 1.16–1.69 倍，比 Self-Forcing 快 1.42–2.92 倍。在 VBench 上，对于 480p 的 1.3B 模型，它取得了更高的分数，并且在更长时长下保持稳定，表明 FlashForward 能以显著更快的生成速度生成时长为 20 秒、35 秒和 65 秒的高质量、时间一致视频。

papers.title: DART: Distillation-Aware Reparameterization for Training-Free LoRA Reuse in Few-Step Video Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: Few-step distillation reduces the inference cost of image-to-video generation, but directly reusing LoRA adapters trained for long denoising trajectories can weaken their intended effects and degrade video quality. We observe that adapters with similar measured static parameter geometry can behave differently under the shortened target schedule, motivating response-aware transfer. We propose DART, a training-free reparameterization method that transports source LoRAs into aligned coordinates through a low-rank distillation bridge. Paired forward evaluations measure channel-level incremental responses under the target schedule to fit coefficients that calibrate response direction, source-relative magnitude, and timestep allocation. Coordinate transport establishes update directions, while calibration adapts their contributions, requiring neither source training videos nor backpropagation. Experiments across multiple distilled I2V models demonstrate improved generation quality and aggregate functional retention over direct reuse. Further analyses show that coordinate transport complements response calibration, with adapter-level benefits encompassing both functional preservation and reduced negative transfer.
papers.summary_cn: Few-step distillation reduces the inference cost of image-to-video generation, but directly reusing LoRA adapters trained for long denoising trajectories can weaken their intended effects and degrade video quality.
papers.contribution_cn: We propose DART, a training-free reparameterization method that transports source LoRAs into aligned coordinates through a low-rank distillation bridge.

papers.title: Where and When to Force: Routed Forcing for Streaming Avatars
papers.abstract: Audio-driven streaming avatar generation requires real-time synthesis of speech-synchronized videos with dynamic and diverse motion. Self Forcing uses Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) to distill bidirectional video diffusion models into causal, few-step generators for real-time streaming. However, DMD minimizes a reverse KL divergence, which is inherently mode-seeking: it causes the student to discard high-dynamic modes and collapse onto static outputs, compressing both dynamics and diversity of generated videos. We find that this collapse is region-heterogeneous: person regions involving pose and gesture variations suffer the largest diversity loss, the audio-driven mouth region shows a small loss, and the background remains nearly stable. Based on this observation, we propose Routed Forcing, which routes the distillation objective by semantic region and noise stage to improve dynamics and diversity while preserving visual quality. Specifically, (1) Where to Force: Semantic-Region Routing applies Data-Forcing Distillation (DFD), which supervises the student with real videos, to the person region where diversity collapse is most severe, while retaining DMD for the mouth and background to preserve lip synchronization and scene stability. (2) When to Force: Noise-Stage Routing activates DFD at high noise stages, where real video serves as effective supervision to inject diverse and dynamic motion patterns. At low noise stages, DMD is used to refine details, avoiding blur and artifacts from spatial differences between real video and student-generated video. Experiments show that Routed Forcing improves dynamics by up to 45% and diversity by 7-25% over Self Forcing, while preserving video quality and lip synchronization.

papers.contribution_cn: Based on this observation, we propose Routed Forcing, which routes the distillation objective by semantic region and noise stage to improve dynamics and diversity while preserving visual quality.

papers.title: UnStep: Training-Free Acceleration of Causal Video Diffusion with Fewer Steps Than Distillation
papers.abstract: Distilling bidirectional multi-step video diffusion transformers into few-step causal models has become a common approach for streaming video generation. While these few-step students are significantly faster than the teachers they are distilled from, they remain slow for real-time generation. In this work we present UnStep, a training-free wrapper that accelerates few-step causal video models at inference by running them with fewer diffusion transformer (DiT) steps than during distillation and limiting the temporal window retained in the attention KV cache. We propose two inference-only mechanisms to recover quality lost by step reduction and attention windowing: renoising the generated latent frames to a near-clean level and reusing the existing clean-cache pass to refine them, and applying truncated SVD to the DiT attention value and output projections. We also accelerate inference with a quality-preserving runtime stack for the DiT and VAE decoder, including more efficient attention calls and KV indexing, fused Triton RoPE with cached coefficients, and VAE decoding with optimized memory layout, precision, and convolution kernels. By reducing computation and optimizing the runtime stack, UnStep sets a new throughput regime for causal video diffusion, by running substantially faster than current methods, reaching 50 FPS on a single H100 without quality loss, and 77 FPS on GB200, all without retraining.

papers.title: OneFixer: High-Quality and Consistent One-Step Autoregressive 3DGS Refinement for Driving Scenes
papers.abstract: Autoregressive video diffusion is a promising render-time fixer for 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) in autonomous-driving simulation, but deployment demands high visual quality and temporal consistency at low latency. This is especially hard for one-step causal generation, where each imperfect prediction immediately becomes context for subsequent frames. Existing approaches stabilize rollouts through staged training with multiple modules and rollout-aware regularization, yet one-step quality still falls short of what deployment requires. We introduce OneFixer, a one-step autoregressive video-diffusion fixer trained in a single task-specific adaptation stage. Our key idea is a deployment-matched shared rollout: the model's own one-step predictions serve as the causal context for flow matching, exposing training to deployment-time errors, while the same rollout receives direct pixel-space perceptual supervision to preserve fine detail. Because the predictions optimized for current-frame quality are exactly those reused as future context, fidelity and autoregressive robustness are learned jointly, without bidirectional-to-causal conversion or teacher-student distillation. OneFixer further exploits cues that driving simulation readily provides, lane geometry and dynamic-agent states, to improve geometric fidelity. On Waymo and proprietary driving scenes with 900-frame rollouts, OneFixer achieves the lowest FVD, LPIPS, and DISTS among all baselines at one step, with temporal consistency matching or exceeding multi-stage DMD pipelines. Under identical backbone and conditioning, it matches a multi-stage DMD-with-Self-Forcing pipeline in under half the GPU-hours and keeps improving beyond its plateau. In closed-loop simulation with a driving policy, OneFixer reduces the collision rate by a third relative to raw 3DGS rendering. Project page: https://onefixer-web.vercel.app/

papers.title: ActionSplice: In-Flight Action Editing for Interactive World Models
papers.abstract: Chunk-autoregressive video world models typically generate each chunk under one action. When an action changes during sampling, waiting until the next chunk delays the response, while directly switching the conditioning leaves the intermediate solver state shaped by the previous action. Restarting sampling under the revised action avoids this mismatch but repeats completed computation. We introduce \emph{ActionSplice}, which edits the interrupted state through Counterfactual State Transport (CST). A lightweight corrector moves the interrupted solver state toward the matched counterfactual solver state induced by the revised action at the same solver step. The world model and sampler remain frozen, and sampling resumes without replaying completed evaluations. $\mathrm{CST}_{R}$ retargets the entire active chunk, while $\mathrm{CST}_{T}$ preserves the temporal prefix at the intervention step and corrects only the suffix. On minWM--Wan Action2V and HY-WM1.5, we measure fidelity against matched rollback references. Relative to condition swapping, $\mathrm{CST}_{R}$ reduces LPIPS by 61.5\% and 75.9\%, and $\mathrm{CST}_{T}$ reduces suffix LPIPS by 56.1\% and 77.5\%, respectively.
papers.summary_cn: Chunk-autoregressive video world models typically generate each chunk under one action.
papers.contribution_cn: We introduce \emph{ActionSplice}, which edits the interrupted state through Counterfactual State Transport (CST).

papers.title: SLIP-VLA: Single-Step Latent Imagination for Policy Learning in Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action models are increasingly effective for robotic manipulation, yet most predict actions directly from current observations without explicitly modeling future scene evolution. Recent methods introduce future prediction to improve action generation, but dense future modeling often requires expensive iterative denoising, while one-step alternatives can underperform their multi-step counterparts. To reconcile efficient future modeling with strong action performance, we present SLIP-VLA, a policy learning framework that equips VLA models with a Single-Step Latent Imagination for future-aware action prediction. SLIP-VLA obtains temporally dense future latent representations with a single denoising update, and we improve the perceptual sufficiency of these representations by aligning intermediate latents with future geometric and semantic features. We further improve their control sufficiency through action-conditioned latent world modeling and inverse dynamics modeling, explicitly coupling latent transitions with robot actions. SLIP-VLA achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse simulation benchmarks and real-world manipulation tasks, while its single-step latent imagination takes only 12 ms.

papers.title: VehDyn: A Driving World Model Benchmark for Vehicle Dynamics
papers.abstract: Video world models are emerging as data engines, action planners, and generative simulators for autonomous driving, but existing benchmarks primarily assess visual fidelity and coarse physical plausibility, providing limited evidence on whether generated driving futures obey realistic vehicle kinematics and dynamics. This limitation is further compounded by the lack of datasets in which vehicle, road, maneuver, and speed conditions are independently controlled, and ground-truth vehicle states are recorded in synchrony with videos. We introduce VehDyn, a driving world model benchmark for vehicle dynamics. VehDyn is built on a CARLA-CarSim co-simulation platform where photorealistic rendering is coupled with a validated multi-body dynamics model, and it contains 10,080 configurations from a full factorial design over five vehicle types, four tire-road friction coefficients, three maneuvers, four target speeds, 14 scenes, and three illuminations, each paired with synchronized position, velocity, and attitude sequences. Built on this dataset, VehDyn introduces a hierarchical evaluation framework that measures trajectory alignment, kinematic consistency, and dynamic consistency, and benchmarks 12 state-of-the-art video world models. We further assess the video quality using two established protocols and correlate it with the VehDyn score. Trajectory-level metrics are nearly saturated, with ten of twelve models within 20\% of ground truth, while no model reaches 92\% of ground truth on dynamic consistency, and visual-quality metrics are only weakly correlated with vehicle-dynamics fidelity. DrivingWorld achieves the highest VehDyn score, followed by Cosmos 3 Nano and LTX-Video 2.5, and the VehDyn score agrees closely with human judgment. VehDyn provides a systematic foundation for developing driving world models that are physically consistent and visually realistic.
